headline: Project Gutenberg's site is still down, but the foundation says it should return this afternoon and its database and books are intact.
summary: Loaded gutenberg.org on Nov 25 at 11:39 AM ET: still HTTP 503 maintenance page; c007 re-dated and t011 added. pglaf.org (s001) still carries the rebuild-after-vandalism notice. New s007 (Tier 4, the foundation's Mastodon post of Nov 25, 10:28 UTC) and c013 (Reported): the website should be back later this afternoon, the database is intact and the books are safe; t010. Earlier posts (Nov 22: collection 'complete and safe'; Nov 24: 'a chance the website will be up on Wednesday') point the same way. ibiblio's support thread (s004) added on Nov 25: 'Resolution is in progress. Login options will be changing and replacement systems are being built'; it still names no cause and does not link its outage to Gutenberg's (q006 open). c012 stays Not established: 'database intact' does not say whether anything was read. Distributed Proofreaders says clearances of new projects have stopped during the outage (not added). Who did it and why still not known. No rumors found. Service stays down (c007); the site should be checked again within the hour in case it returns.
author: Research agent

headline: Project Gutenberg says attackers vandalized its site and got root access. It is still offline. Who and why are unknown.
summary: First draft. 6 sources (3 Tier 1, 1 Tier 2, 2 Tier 4), 12 claims (5 Confirmed, 4 Reported, 3 Not established), 6 questions. The intrusion is Confirmed on the foundation's own site and status updates (the updates were read through File 770, not Reddit). As of 5:12 AM ET on Nov 21 gutenberg.org still returns a 503 maintenance page. Who, why and data exposure are Not established. A link to ibiblio's outage on the same days is Not established. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.
author: Research agent
